tagline: Teak houses and indigo-dyed cloth, an old town to wander slowly
introHtml: Phrae is a small northern town that most people just drive through on the way to Nan or Chiang Rai. But stop and you'll find an old town that has kept a lot of its handsome teak-wood houses, from the former ruler's residence to old noble homes. The town is known for teak and for hom dyed cloth, indigo-dyed and made here for generations. Around town there's Wat Phra That Cho Hae as the city's guardian temple, and Phae Mueang Phi where the earth has eroded into strange, otherworldly shapes. If you like a town that isn't crowded and is easy to stroll, Phrae is more enjoyable than you'd expect.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable, great for walking the old town and visiting temples

highlights.name: Mo Hom indigo cloth
highlights.blurb: The deep-blue indigo-dyed cloth that Phrae is known for. The Ban Thung Hong community has made and sold it for ages, and you can pick up mo hom shirts to take home.

highlights.name: Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae
highlights.blurb: The teak mansion of the last local ruler, built in a European-Lanna mix. The whole house is beautiful old architecture and one of the town's defining images.

highlights.name: Wat Phra That Cho Hae
highlights.blurb: Phrae's guardian stupa on a low hill, the year-of-the-tiger stupa. Locals and visitors alike come to pay respects all year round.

highlights.name: Phrae old town
highlights.blurb: The area inside the old city walls still has its moat, teak houses, old temples, and small cafes to stroll around at an easy pace.

highlights.name: Phae Mueang Phi
highlights.blurb: A landscape of soil and rock eroded by rain into columns and cliffs in odd shapes. Walking through it feels like another world.

highlights.name: Wongburi House
highlights.blurb: An old pink teak gingerbread house belonging to the family of the town's rulers, with fine fretwork detailing. Open to visitors.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, kaeng hang le, sai ua, found all over town with proper northern flavors.

foodScene.name: Khanom sen nam sai and nam ngiao
foodScene.note: Rice noodles with nam ngiao or clear broth are a breakfast that Phrae locals eat regularly, served with vegetables and crispy pork rind.

foodScene.name: Khao khaep and khao khuap
foodScene.note: Thin sheets of dough grilled until crisp, a local Phrae snack you can also buy to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Sai ua and crispy pork rind
foodScene.note: A side dish and gift that goes with the north, eaten with sticky rice or carried home.

foodScene.name: Sukhothai noodles and local noodles
foodScene.note: Phrae borders Sukhothai, so there are noodle shops with the bold peanut-and-lime flavor alongside the usual northern places.

foodScene.name: Cafes in the old town
foodScene.note: The old town has several cafes set in wooden houses and old homes, good for sipping coffee in a quiet setting.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for Phrae locals, with plenty of spots to choose from at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Morning markets and town markets
foodScene.note: Fresh markets in town have rice-and-curry plates, local vegetables, and regional sweets to sample at local prices.

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Cho Hae
attractions.blurb: The town's guardian stupa on a hill, the year-of-the-tiger stupa, a key place to pay respects that visitors to Phrae shouldn't miss.

attractions.name: Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae
attractions.blurb: The teak mansion of the last local ruler in a European-Lanna mix, beautiful old architecture to walk through.

attractions.name: Wongburi House
attractions.blurb: An old pink teak gingerbread house with fine fretwork detailing, open to view inside.

attractions.name: Ban Prathap Jai (Hundred-Pillar House)
attractions.blurb: A large teak house built with a hundred whole teak posts, showing off the beauty of Phrae's teak wood.

attractions.name: Phae Mueang Phi
attractions.blurb: Soil and rock eroded into columns and cliffs in odd shapes, a nature walk unlike anywhere else.

attractions.name: Phrae old town and Pratu Chai
attractions.blurb: The area inside the old city walls with its moat, where you can walk past teak houses, old temples, and small cafes.

attractions.name: Wat Chom Sawan
attractions.blurb: A Tai Yai-style temple built entirely of wood, with fretwork and old pieces kept on display.

attractions.name: Wiang Kosai National Park and Mae Koeng Waterfall
attractions.blurb: Green forest and clear, cool waterfalls in the west of the province, good for hikers and a dip.
